corpus: ENCYCLOPEDIA (Wikipedia), not arXiv -- testing whether obscure low-ML-overlap concepts break the arXiv saturation (~21 hits/query, Run 16-20)
method: WebSearch 'wikipedia <concept>' returns a verbatim summary (R9; WebFetch 403s). Decomposed each into mechanism atoms (verbatim, R5). 2 tiers x 3 concepts x 2 atoms = 12.
verbatim_note: Each atom text is a mechanism sentence/clause from the Wikipedia summary as WebSearch rendered it this session (clean text). Titles/URLs verbatim from Links. No text invented.
queries_used: wikipedia entropy thermodynamics statistical mechanics disorder microstates definition
wikipedia game theory Nash equilibrium strategic interaction payoff definition

wikipedia retting flax fiber separation process

atoms.sub_mechanism: entropy = number of ways a system can be arranged (disorder)
atoms.text: In statistical mechanics, entropy is a measure of the number of ways a system can be arranged, often taken to be a measure of disorder; the higher the entropy, the higher the disorder.

atoms.sub_mechanism: entropy quantifies how many microstates are consistent with a given macrostate
atoms.text: A microstate is one specific arrangement of all the particles in a system; many different microstates can correspond to the same macrostate, and entropy quantifies how many microstates are consistent with a given macrostate.

atoms.sub_mechanism: Nash equilibrium: no player can improve payoff by unilaterally changing strategy
atoms.text: A Nash equilibrium is a set of strategies, one for each player, such that no player can improve their payoff by unilaterally changing their strategy.

atoms.sub_mechanism: decision-making as strategic interaction based on the actions of other players
atoms.text: Decision-making is a system of strategic interactions based on the actions of other players, used to analyze the outcome of the strategic interaction of several decision makers.

atoms.sub_mechanism: differential survival and reproduction due to differences in relative fitness
atoms.text: Natural selection is the differential survival and reproduction of individuals due to differences in the relative fitness endowed on them by their own particular complement of observable characteristics.

If you have variation, differential reproduction, and heredity, you will have evolution by natural selection as an outcome; advantageous variations are preserved and multiplied at the expense of less-advantageous ones.

atoms.sub_mechanism: separating bast fibre from non-fibrous materials
atoms.text: Retting is a textile process for separating the bast fibre in plants from the non-fibrous materials to create fibers that can be spun into yarn.

atoms.sub_mechanism: microbial or chemical degradation of the cementing compounds that bind the fibres
atoms.text: The separation is primarily achieved through either a microbial or chemical action degradating the cementing compounds that bind the bast fibres to other plant tissues, allowing the fibers to be isolated.

atoms.sub_mechanism: refraction of swells on undersea slopes and bending of swells around islands
atoms.text: Navigators mainly concentrated on refraction of swells as they came in contact with undersea slopes of islands and the bending of swells around islands as they interacted with swells coming from opposite directions.

atoms.sub_mechanism: a complex interference pattern localizes a distant hidden island 20-30 miles away
atoms.text: As a wave approaches an island the shoreline refracts it, and this interaction creates a complex interference pattern, an area of choppy confused water, that can be felt in a canoe up to 20-30 miles away from the island causing it.

atoms.sub_mechanism: alkalinity dissolves hemicellulose, the glue-like component binding the cell walls
atoms.text: The alkalinity helps the dissolution of hemicellulose, the major glue-like component of the maize cell walls, and loosens the hulls from the kernels and softens the maize.

atoms.sub_mechanism: selective transformation: solubilizes some components while swelling others
atoms.text: Cooking and steeping maize in lime solution at pH above 11 softens the pericarp, hydrates the endosperm, partially solubilizes proteins and cell walls, facilitates starch swelling, and gelatinizes only a small amount of starch.
